LESSON: SCHOOL ADMINISTRATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Social Organisations
Topic 2.4: School administration

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on School administration. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is school administration organised?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify administrative leaders in a school
2. state duties of administrative leaders in a school
3. appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school
4. identify resources found in Kenya
5. explain the benefits of using available resources prudently
6. appreciate the resources available in society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SCHOOL ADMINISTRATION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
School administration helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: SCHOOL ADMINISTRATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify administrative leaders in a school

What this means
In this part you learn to identify administrative leaders in a school. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify administrative leaders in a school.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “School administration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify administrative leaders in a school. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: State duties of administrative leaders in a school

What this means
In this part you learn to state duties of administrative leaders in a school. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: state duties of administrative leaders in a school.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to School administration.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can state duties of administrative leaders in a school. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Identify resources found in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify resources found in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify resources found in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “School administration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify resources found in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Explain the benefits of using available resources prudently

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the benefits of using available resources prudently. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the benefits of using available resources prudently.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to School administration.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the benefits of using available resources prudently. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Appreciate the resources available in society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the resources available in society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the resources available in society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the resources available in society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what School administration is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “School administration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify administrative leaders in a school)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to School administration. (skill: state duties of administrative leaders in a school)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school)

Example 4: Connect “School administration” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify resources found in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach School administration to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify administrative leaders in a school.
3. Practise this skill: state duties of administrative leaders in a school.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate work done by administrative leaders in school.
5. Make one local Kenya example of School administration from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for School administration: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study School administration?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is school administration organised?
2. Why is it important to use resources prudently?
3. How can we conserve resources in our society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what School administration means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify administrative leaders in a school.
5. Be able to: state duties of administrative leaders in a school.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
